title: Sheaf-theoretic Smith theory, parity sheaves and Satake base change
summary: Construct the Smith restriction functor from equivariant étale sheaves to a cyclic Tate quotient, its relative localization and six-operation comparisons, and the normalized integral Tate-parity lifting used in cyclic Satake base change. The final comparison identifies this functor with diagonal restriction of tilting representations under modular equal-characteristic geometric Satake. The plan separates valid ordinary coefficient reduction from false equivariant fullness, character equality from natural dual-group equivariance, and objectwise integral comparisons from their unresolved naturality. It also owns the general algebra Tate diagonal and Frobenius linearization needed by the global and local consumers.
readme:
## Aim

Construct cyclic Smith restriction and its parity-lifting refinement to the Satake base change functor. The endpoint is Feng Theorem 4.20: Sat_H BC is naturally isomorphic to restriction along the diagonal Ĥ→Ĥ^p composed with Sat_G on normalized parity sheaves, identified with tilting representations. Also export the general algebra Tate diagonal and character-extension theorem to the global and local consumers.

## Conventions

F is separably closed of characteristic different from the odd prime p, k=overline(F_p), O=W(k), G=H^p and σ cyclically rotates the factors. Require p good for the dual root system for parity–tilting and the final comparison. Sheaf functors are enhanced étale operations on bounded-dimensional finite-type supports; adic systems retain uniform Tor/cohomological bounds. Geometric equivariance differs from a coefficient action. Normalized CT uses [⟨2ρ,ν⟩], and inverse Frobenius is applied on the source of the semilinear functor.

## Layers

ST.0 specifies actions, coefficients and Tor bounds. ST.1 constructs Tate quotients and cohomology. ST.2 constructs Smith operations and localization. ST.3 supplies the missing modular equal-characteristic Satake branch. ST.4 constructs parity, Tate parity and normalized lifting. ST.5 builds the norm and linear BC. ST.6 proves constant-term comparisons and identifies the natural diagonal-restriction proof obligation. ST.7 treats exactness, descent and the valid integral comparison. ST.8 exports the algebra diagonal and Frobenius linearization.

## Sources and ownership

The main source is Feng, Smith theory and cyclic base change functoriality, Forum Math. Pi 12 (2024), e1, §§3–4 and Appendix A, with exact theorem/page locators in the packet and reader. Leslie–Lonergan, Juteau–Mautner–Williamson, Mautner–Riche, Mirković–Vilonen and Braden supply the recorded parity, Satake and localization inputs. Existing enhanced sheaves, torsion six operations, equal-characteristic Grassmannian geometry, integral dual groups and upstream rational representations remain supplier imports. Weyl and induced modules and the good-filtration tensor theorem are requested from the integral highest-weight extension of Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 9 (DESIGN-ReductiveGroupsPartIII), the owner LanglandsParameterStacks also imports them from. Treumann–Venkatesh §§2.1 and 3.4 are special cases of ST.8. This roadmap does not replan root data, B_dR^+ Satake, module-level Tate cohomology or downstream shtuka/local Langlands applications.

All 63 routed items are assigned. This is a complete target-level plan with all nine stages planned and G1–G5 explicit; no stage is closed. Full definitions, APIs, worked Checks and remaining proof obligations are in research/blueprint/readmes/SheafTheoreticSmithTheory.md.

stages.title: Actions, coefficients and finite Tor dimension
stages.description: Specify the odd-prime coefficient datum, admissible geometric cyclic actions, fixed schemes and enhanced quotient-stack equivariance. Distinguish geometric equivariance from group-ring coefficients on a trivial action. Prove arbitrary flat modules over the cyclic group ring in characteristic p are free, and state the uniform stalkwise Tor-amplitude/flat-resolution criterion. Reuse the existing Witt-vector, derived-category and enhanced sheaf carriers.

stages.title: Tate categories and relative Tate cohomology
stages.description: Construct the bounded constructible and uniformly bounded ind-constructible cyclic Tate Verdier quotients on a trivially acted-on space. Prove categorical two-periodicity and define sheaf-valued periodic Tate cohomology, its long exact sequence and the trivial k/O-action formulas. Specify the stratified integral quotient and inflation. Distinguish categorical periodicity from the existing module-level Tate isomorphism; the W(k)-adic conservative comparison requires G1.

stages.title: Smith operations and localization
stages.description: Prove the separate uniform finite-Tor bounds for Rf! and ambient Rj*, extend compact support to bounded-dimensional locally finite-type maps, and use free geometric quotients to compare fixed ! and * restrictions. Construct Psm=T*i* with its ! presentation, descended six operations on their specified domains, compact-pushforward compatibility and relative Tate localization. Keep the adic extension G1 visible and check every construction on bounded pieces.

stages.title: The modular equal-characteristic Satake branch
stages.description: Construct the missing equal-characteristic modular geometric Satake equivalence with fusion symmetry, k/O-flat coefficient change and the standard/costandard comparison. Reuse integral dual groups and rational representation carriers. Define rational tilting representations from the Weyl and induced modules requested from the integral highest-weight extension of Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 9, prove tensor closure and bounded derived generation via finite highest-weight ideals. This is the modular scheme-theoretic branch, not a duplicate of the B_dR^+ Satake roadmap.

stages.title: Parity, Tate parity and lifting
stages.description: Give JMW stratifications, ordinary parity, support uniqueness and Grassmannian parity existence/equivariance. Prove good-prime perversity and the parity–tilting equivalence, with the MR exotic/Soergel engine isolated as G3 and étale transport as G2. Construct integral Tate parity, the graded Hom formula with composition and the normalized degree-zero lifting functor. Prove ordinary parity coefficient reduction; exclude the false full C_p-equivariant equivalence.

stages.title: The norm and the base change functor
stages.description: Identify the fixed Grassmannian of H^p with Gr_H, define the cyclic convolution norm and prove its normalized parity stalk/costalk criterion. Show Smith sends this norm to normalized integral Tate parity. Establish additivity and Frobenius semilinearity on morphisms through induced mixed terms. Specify the prime-field form, category twist and inverse-source-Frobenius linearization, then construct the additive k-linear BC functor using only ordinary parity reduction.

stages.title: Constant terms and diagonal restriction
stages.description: Construct equal-characteristic monodromic hyperbolic localization and normalized constant terms, including extreme semi-infinite intersections. Prove the CT/Satake, CT/Smith and CT/lifting squares on objects and morphisms. Compute torus BC. Obtain equality of tilting characters and isomorphism classes under diagonal restriction, then state the additional root-group/naturality obligation G5 needed for the natural isomorphism Sat_H BC≅Res_Δ Sat_G of Feng Theorem 4.20.

stages.title: Exactness, descent and integral comparison
stages.description: Prove CT conservative on the constructible monodromic k-Tate domain, and the exact-triangle property of Smith composed with norm on short exact Satake sequences. Construct continuous equivariantization and the Galois compatibility of BC, with a genuinely equivariant natural comparison required for L-group descent. Retain the valid objectwise integral comparison and separately require its natural norm-image version G4; do not claim a natural identity on all integral Tate maps.

stages.title: The Tate diagonal of an algebra
stages.description: Construct the transfer ideal in the fixed subring of a commutative F_p-algebra and prove that the norm class is the additive/multiplicative Tate diagonal. Reuse module-level H0 and character independence, prove the unique extension of a transfer-annihilating character to a perfect field, and formulate Frobenius twists of vector spaces and algebras and source linearization relative to a specified F_p-form. The Treumann–Venkatesh twist of a vector space and their bijection on σ-fixed characters are the special cases imported by SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality. This general algebra input is shared by the global and local consumers.
